name: viewer_state
description: Everything about the active layer (and the list of layers): point count, local and global bounds, the global shift, median point spacing, what fraction of points carry a real normal, the scalar field, the reconstructed surface (triangles, vertices, holeRatio = boundary edges / triangles, the voxel it was built at), station count, the cloud transform, unsaved work, the camera record — and recommendedSource, which says whether to measure the points or the surface, and why. Units are metres throughout. Start here.

name: viewer_view
description: A calibrated image. With a preset it is rendered with a true orthographic projection, so one metre is the same number of pixels everywhere and the mapping that comes back turns any pixel into a world point exactly: topLeft plus perPixelRight/perPixelDown, or originX/originY/extentX/extentY for the axis-aligned presets. Use this, not viewer_screenshot, for anything you intend to measure. Set ortho:false for an ordinary perspective look from that direction. The current colour mode is respected, so a scalar field photographs as itself.

ortho.description: default true for a preset: orthographic and measurable

name: viewer_section
description: A floor plan or a wall elevation: an orthographic image of one slab only, with the same exact pixel-to-metre mapping. axis is the slab normal, at is where it sits (metres, local frame — take it from viewer_state bounds), thickness is how deep. The rest of the cloud is hidden for the render and put back afterwards.

at.description: default the middle of the bounds

thickness.description: metres, default about eight point spacings

name: viewer_probe
description: Turn pixels of the most recent viewer_view or viewer_section back into world points, local and global. That render's camera is re-established first, so the answer is exact even if the view has moved since. null where the pixel hit nothing.

pixels.description: [[x,y], …] in the pixels of that image

name: viewer_heightmap
description: A raster of the highest surface per cell, as a grey PNG, with its metre mapping. Grey 0 means no data; 1..255 maps linearly onto [zMin, zMax]. Computed from a uniform sample, so it is fast on tens of millions of points.

axis.description: which axis is measured; z is a height model

resolution.description: cells along the longer side, default 512

name: viewer_contour
description: The footprint of a horizontal slab as 2D polylines in metres (local frame; add translation for global), traced by marching squares over an occupancy raster and simplified. This is the primitive to draw a plan from — vectors, not a picture.

z.description: slab centre in metres, local frame

dilate.description: grow the raster by a cell first; use on a sparse or patchy scan

maxVertices.description: simplification is loosened until the result fits, default 12000

name: viewer_fitplane
description: Best-fit plane through the points inside a box (or through points you supply) by PCA: normal, centroid, RMS and worst distance, dip and dip direction in degrees, and how many points it used. RMS is how flat the thing actually is — the number that says whether to trust the plane.

name: viewer_distance
description: Straight-line distance between two world points, with the height difference and the horizontal component. Metres.

name: viewer_inside
description: Exact count and bounding box of the points inside a box. Exact, not sampled: cells wholly inside are counted without being read, only the cells the box cuts are.

name: viewer_screenshot
description: The current view as a PNG, plus the camera record (position, target, up, fov, aspect, pixel size, view-projection matrix) so nothing you are shown is uncalibrated. For anything measurable prefer viewer_view, which is orthographic.

name: viewer_set_view
description: Move the camera. preset: fit | top; or give pose {p:[x,y,z], t:[x,y,z]} (local metres, Z up); or fly {position, yaw, pitch}. Returns a screenshot.

name: viewer_set
description: Change display settings. Any subset: colorMode (0 rgb,1 intensity,2 rgb×intensity,3 elevation,4 normals,5 scalar field,6 flat), pointSize, maxPx, edl, edlStrength, normalShade, budget, density, clipZMin, clipZMax, bright, gamma.

name: viewer_regions
description: Bounding shapes that decide what survives: box, sphere, slab, or prism (an outline extruded along a view direction). The usual way to make one is place: point at a thing (a world point, or a pixel of the last view) and get a small box or sphere centred exactly there, then grow it by a factor or fit it to what it holds. role keep = crop to the union of the keeps; delete = remove what is inside. lasso is the shortcut for a prism: give screen pixels from the current camera and it builds the region the way the panel does, reporting how many points it holds. mode sets which way the panel's own crop region cuts. apply commits every keep and delete region in one undoable step. A region is not a cut until apply, so it can be inspected from any angle first.

poly.description: prism: the outline in the region's own local XY plane, metres, extruded to +/- half[2] along local Z

at.description: op=place: where to put it, local metres

pixel.description: op=place: a pixel of the last view instead

factor.description: op=grow: multiply the active region by this

role.description: op=mode or op=lasso: keep inside, or remove inside

pixels.description: op=lasso: [[x,y], …] of the image you measured

height.description: op=lasso: the pixel size of that image, if it was not the live canvas

depth.description: op=lasso: half depth along the view axis in metres; the default spans the cloud

name: viewer_pick
description: World point under a screen pixel (x,y in CSS px of the last screenshot scale), or null.

name: viewer_measure
description: Distance between two world points, or between two picked pixels.

name: viewer_export
description: Export the points in memory to a local file on this machine. format e57|las|ply, stride keeps 1 in N.

name: viewer_open
description: Open a scan. In the desktop app give `path`, a file on this machine (E57, LAS, LAZ, PLY, PTX, OBJ, STL or delimited text), with add:true to bring it in as another layer instead of replacing what is open. In a browser tab there is no file system, so it is a cached scan by key (as listed by viewer_state.cached, Chromium only) or a cloud scan by id.

path.description: desktop only: a file on this machine

add.description: open as another layer rather than replacing what is open

name: viewer_cache
description: The on-device cache of decoded cells. A scan that took thirteen seconds to decode reopens from this in about one, so caching a scan you will come back to is the single biggest thing an agent can do for the next session. list reports what is cached with point counts; write caches the scan now in memory, including any crop and transform, under a key derived from the file; drop removes one. Open a cached scan with viewer_open cached:<key>. Chromium and the desktop app only — it is OPFS underneath.

key.description: op=drop: which cached scan, default the one open

name: viewer_surface
description: Reconstruct a triangle mesh from the points and their normals, show or hide it, discard it, or write it to a file on this machine. The viewer calls the result a mesh and the operation surface reconstruction; viewer_mesh measures and edits whatever this produces. build takes voxelCm (detail, smaller is finer), smooth (0-6) and fillGaps (1-4), and reports holeRatio so you can tell whether the result is worth measuring. export writes PLY or OBJ to `path` with the cloud transform and the global shift already baked in. The points are never modified.

name: viewer_script
description: Run several commands in order on the tab in one call, with each step's result available to the next. The round trip is the expensive part of driving a viewer, and most steps are decided entirely by the previous answer, so sending the plan once turns twenty waits into one. Each step is { cmd, args, save?, label? } and args may hold variables: $last is the previous step's result, $layers and $active are refreshed before every step, and a step with save:"name" binds its own result under that name. Dotted paths index in — "$last.area", "$layers.0.id", "$s.bounds.local.centre" — and ${...} inside a longer string interpolates. Replies list every step in order with its result, its error and its time. stopOnError defaults to true. A step that answers with a picture reports the size instead of the bytes: ask for pictures with their own view or screenshot call.

vars.description: variables available to the first step

name: viewer_mesh
description: Triangle meshes as layers. A mesh opened in the viewer (Mesh -> Import a mesh…, PLY/OBJ/STL) becomes a layer of its own, drawn alongside the clouds and moved by viewer_transform like one; every visible layer's triangles are drawn, not only the active one's. list reports the mesh layers. measure gives surface area and volume through the layer's transform, with the boundary edge count next to them — volume only means anything when closed is true, and an open mesh says so rather than quietly returning a number. sample scatters points over the triangles, area-weighted, into a NEW point layer with normals and colours (give count or density in points per m2). distance measures every point of the ACTIVE CLOUD to the nearest TRIANGLE of a mesh layer — point-to-triangle, not point-to-nearest-vertex — and writes it as a scalar field. flip reverses the winding. smooth is Taubin by default, which keeps the volume, or plain Laplacian with taubin:false, which shrinks it. decimate is vertex clustering at cellCm, which is fast but cannot hit an exact triangle count. save writes PLY, OBJ or STL to a path on this machine, with the layer transform and the global shift baked in.

count.description: op=sample: how many points in all

density.description: op=sample: points per square metre, instead of count

mesh.description: op=distance: the mesh layer id or name

signed.description: op=distance: report which side of the surface each point is on

taubin.description: op=smooth: keep the volume, default true

cellCm.description: op=decimate: clustering cell in centimetres, default 10

name: viewer_entities
description: The clouds in memory. Every visible one is drawn; exactly one is active, and every other tool — crop, analysis, surface, transform, export — works on the active one. list reports them with their point counts and transforms; activate switches; show/hide toggles drawing without unloading; rename; clone copies the active one; merge appends every other visible layer into the active one through each of their transforms (scalar fields are dropped, and it cannot be undone); remove unloads one. A file is added in the viewer itself (Layers -> Add file…) or with viewer_open for a cached scan.

id.description: the layer id or its name

name: viewer_register
description: Move the ACTIVE layer onto a reference layer; the reference is never touched. centres matches bounding-box centres, scales matches their sizes (for two clouds in different units — not for a rotated copy, whose boxes legitimately differ), and icp is point-to-plane fine registration, reporting per-iteration RMS, final RMS, overlap fraction and the matrix. Each is one undoable transform step.

reference.description: the id or name of another layer

maxDistance.description: op=icp: rejection gate as a multiple of three point spacings, default 6

name: viewer_distance_to
description: Distance from every point of the ACTIVE layer to the nearest point of a reference layer, written as a scalar field named "Distance to <reference>" — so the colour ramp, the histogram and the value filter all work on it. signed projects onto the reference point's own normal instead, which says which side of the reference surface each point is on: settlement and heave stop cancelling into the same positive number. A reference bigger than the analyser holds is subsampled, and the reply says so.

name: viewer_volume
description: A 2.5D volume between the ACTIVE layer and a reference — another layer, or a flat plane at a height. Reports added (fill), removed (cut) and net separately, because their sum hides both, plus the area it covered. The reference is hole-filled first and the active layer is not: a cell the reference has no point in still has ground under it, but filling the active layer would invent surface past its own edge. Draws the difference as a coloured grid.

reference.description: a layer id or name; omit or "plane" for a flat plane

plane.description: the plane height in local metres, when there is no reference layer

name: viewer_fit
description: Fit a primitive to the ACTIVE REGION's contents, or to the whole layer when no region is active — or give a box and it fits inside that. Returns the parameters and the RMS, which is the number that decides whether to believe them: a cylinder fitted to a flat wall has a radius and an axis and means nothing, and only the residual says so. The fitted shape is drawn in the view.

name: viewer_detect
description: Find shapes without being told where: RANSAC over the points, one shape at a time, removing each shape's inliers before looking for the next. Returns the shapes with their parameters, point counts and RMS, and writes a scalar field named "Shape" holding each point's shape index — so the ramp shows them and the value filter isolates one.

tolerance.description: metres a point may be from a shape and still belong to it, default 0.02

name: viewer_analysis
description:
Neighbourhood analysis and cleaning on the ACTIVE layer. Every op is one undoable step.

normals estimates a normal per point from its neighbours and, unless orient:false, turns each one toward the nearest scanner station — the only orientation that is right for something scanned from the inside. invert flips them. feature writes one of fifteen geometric measures as a scalar field: roughness, curvature, planarity, linearity, sphericity, anisotropy, omnivariance, eigenentropy, verticality, volume_density, surface_density, neighbours, eig1, eig2, eig3. components labels groups of points that touch within radius, as a field, so one cluster can be isolated with the value filter.

The four that remove points: sor and noise are CloudCompare's SOR and noise filters, reimplemented so the same settings remove the same points. sor measures each point's mean distance to its knn nearest neighbours and drops those beyond mean + nSigma standard deviations, over the whole cloud — one global threshold, so be aware that a few very distant points raise it far enough to let nearer outliers through. noise fits a plane to the points AROUND each point and drops the point if it sits further off that plane than its neighbours' own spread allows, so the threshold is local: smooth areas are judged strictly and rough ones loosely. Its neighbourhood is a sphere of radius (CloudCompare's default) or the knn nearest; its threshold is relative (nSigma of the local spread) or an absolute distance; and points with fewer than three neighbours are kept unless removeIsolated is set, because "too few points to judge" is not the same as "noise". duplicates drops points within tolerance of an earlier one. subsample keeps one point per cube of spacing.

Size: a cloud too big to index in one go is analysed one spatial tile at a time, each tile holding its own points plus a halo of its neighbours', so the answer is the same as it would be whole. The reply carries tiles when that happened. sor takes two passes over the tiles, because its threshold is the mean and standard deviation of the whole cloud. components is the one op that still needs every point in one index, and it says so if the cloud is past what this device can hold.

neighbours.description: k for normals, feature, sor, and noise in knn mode. CloudCompare's filter dialogs default to 8.

nSigma.description: op=sor, and op=noise with a relative threshold. Default 1.0, as in CloudCompare.

orient.description: op=normals: turn normals toward the scanner stations. Default true.

radius.description: metres: the neighbourhood for feature and components, and for noise in radius mode

minPoints.description: op=components: the smallest cluster worth labelling

absoluteError.description: op=noise with an absolute threshold: metres from the local plane

removeIsolated.description: op=noise: drop points with too few neighbours to fit a plane. Default false, as in CloudCompare.

name: viewer_transform
description: Move, rotate, scale or level the whole cloud. The points are never rewritten: the cloud carries a 4x4 matrix applied at render, test, analysis and export time, so this is instant, lossless and undoable, and only a written file bakes it. get reports the matrix; set replaces it (16 numbers, row-major); translate/rotate/scale compose on top of it; level fits a plane to a sample and turns it horizontal; reset clears it.

about.description: op=rotate/scale pivot, default the bounding-box centre

name: viewer_history
description: Undo or redo the last edit, save a copy of the in-memory cloud (clears undo/redo), or report stack status.

name: viewer_stations
description: List panorama stations, or enter one by index to look around its 360° photo (exit with index -1).

name: viewer_log
description: What has been run against this viewer tab, newest first, over every path: this MCP bridge, an HTTP session, or a script. Each entry carries the time, where the call came from, the command, its arguments, whether it needed the edit permission, whether it succeeded, how long it took and a trimmed copy of the reply. Read-only, and nothing is stored anywhere but the tab's memory: the last 500 calls, gone when the tab closes. Useful for picking up a session someone else started, for seeing what a script actually did, and for putting the sequence that led to a problem into a bug report.

limit.description: How many of the most recent entries to return. Default 20.

replies.description: Include each entry's reply. Default false, because the replies are much larger than the calls.
